name: Microscopic
description: Atoms, DNA, viruses, cells and grains of sand: things far too small to see, drawn next to things you know.

name: Everyday objects
description: Coins, cards, phones, paper and shipping containers: familiar objects measured to their official specifications.

name: Animals
description: From an ant to the largest animal that has ever lived: how big animals really are next to a person.

name: Prehistoric
description: Dinosaurs, Megalodon and woolly mammoths. Their sizes are estimates from fossils, so they are shown as ranges.

name: Sports
description: Balls, courts, pitches, rinks and pools, measured to the official rules of each sport.

name: Vehicles
description: Cars, buses, trucks, airliners, airships and ships, drawn to scale so you can see how they measure up.

name: Buildings
description: Homes and skyscrapers compared at their true heights, from a family house to the tallest buildings in the world.

name: Structures
description: Towers, monuments, bridges, dams and stadiums: famous structures measured and drawn side by side.

name: Nature
description: The tallest trees, great waterfalls, the highest mountains and the deepest trench, measured against familiar things.

name: Space
description: Spacecraft, planets, the Sun, giant stars and whole galaxies, from metres to hundreds of thousands of light-years across.
